items.q: Four parts of the urinary system?
items.a: Paired kidneys, paired ureters, urinary bladder, urethra
Kidney → ureter → bladder (enters dorsal aspect) → urethra

items.q: Cavities the urinary system lies in?
items.a: Abdominal and pelvic cavities

items.q: Why is it called the urogenital system?
items.a: Shares the urethra: runs through the penis in males, joins the vagina in females
Form urine from the blood

items.q: Large dog: daily renal blood flow and urine output?
items.a: 1000 to 2000 liters of blood → 1 to 2 liters of urine
Regulates blood pressure (renin-angiotensin system); spelled with a single n
Increases red blood cell production in bone marrow
Pressed against the abdominal roof, lumbar region, right and left of median plane
Retroperitoneal (behind the peritoneum)

items.q: Which kidney surface has peritoneum, and which layer?
items.a: Ventral surface only, parietal peritoneum (no visceral peritoneum)

items.q: Which kidney is fixed, which is pendulous?
items.a: Right is fixed (less variable); left is pendulous (more variable)

items.q: Which kidney is more cranial, and by how much?
items.a: Right, by about half a kidney length
Thirteenth thoracic or first lumbar vertebra to third lumbar vertebra
Second lumbar to fourth lumbar vertebra
“Left behind”: the left kidney is more caudal
items.why: Professor's own mnemonic for cranial-versus-caudal kidney questions

items.q: How to palpate the right kidney on physical exam?
items.a: Find the last (floating) rib, then go dorsally
Unilobar (smooth, papillae fused into a crest)

items.q: Kidney type with lobes visible on the surface?
items.a: Multilobar (cow)
Multilobar; fused lobes become unilobar
Convex; abdominal wall, and spleen on the left
Concave (indented, forms the hilus)

items.q: Right kidney medial border faces the…
items.a: Caudal vena cava

items.q: Left kidney medial border faces the…
items.a: Abdominal aorta
Contacts lumbar hypaxial muscles; free of peritoneum
Faces the abdominal cavity; covered by parietal peritoneum

items.q: Gland at the cranial pole of both kidneys?
items.a: Adrenal (suprarenal) gland

items.q: Right kidney cranial pole contacts the…
items.a: Caudate process of the liver (renal impression) and right adrenal gland

items.q: Left kidney cranial pole contacts the…
items.a: Left lobe of the pancreas and left adrenal gland

items.q: Right kidney caudal pole contacts the…
items.a: Ascending colon

items.q: Left kidney caudal pole contacts the…
items.a: Descending colon, and mesovarium in females
Part of the broad ligament suspending the ovary
Indented medial border of the kidney

items.q: Structures entering or leaving at the hilus?
items.a: Renal artery, renal vein, lymphatics, nerves, ureter
Recess (space) the hilus leads into
Renal pelvis, fat, proximal branches of renal vessels and nerves
Driveway = vessels · garage door = hilus · garage = sinus
Funnel-shaped dilatation of the ureter inside the renal sinus (the “sea”)

items.q: Renal pelvis receives urine from… and passes it to…
items.a: From papillary ducts; into the ureter
Curved diverticula of the renal pelvis (the “rivers” feeding the sea)
Into the parenchyma between renal pyramids
5 to 6 from each border of the pelvis
Entire kidney surface (not peritoneum)
Mostly collagen, few elastic fibers
Kidney cannot swell well when internal pressure rises

items.q: Why does the capsule strip easily from a healthy kidney?
items.a: Attached by loose connective tissue

items.q: Capsule that won't peel off at necropsy means…
items.a: Adhesions or pathology (fibrosis)
Outer parenchyma, just inside the fibrous capsule

items.q: Why does the cortex look granular?
items.a: Renal corpuscles (glomeruli), found only in the cortex
Inner, darker parenchyma

items.q: Why does the medulla look striated?
items.a: Medullary rays
Cut through the midline dividing the kidney into equal halves
Free (shelf-like) edge of the medulla facing the pelvis
Fusion of the renal papillae
On the border of the renal crest facing the pelvis
Papillary foramina (not visible grossly)
Apex of the renal pyramid
Pyramid-shaped medullary substance; represents a kidney lobe

items.q: Seen ONLY in a paramedian section?
items.a: Renal pyramids and renal papillae
items.why: Professor put a star on these two: paramedian sections only

items.a: Cut parallel to and slightly off the midline
Aorta → renal → interlobar → arcuate → interlobular → afferent arteriole → efferent arteriole
Cortical capillary plexus and medullary capillary plexus

items.q: Vessels supplying the medullary capillary plexus?
items.a: Straight arteries; drained by straight veins
Interlobular → arcuate → interlobar → renal vein → caudal vena cava

items.q: Blood supply chain the professor cares about?
items.a: Abdominal aorta → renal artery → arcuate arteries … renal vein → caudal vena cava
items.why: “These you must know” / “that's all I care about” (outlined vessels)

items.q: Arcuate arteries are located at the…
items.a: Corticomedullary junction
They form an arc
Narrow muscular tube carrying urine from kidney to bladder

items.q: How does the ureter move urine?
items.a: Smooth muscle peristalsis (little help from gravity in quadrupeds)
Size of the animal
Abdominal part and pelvic part

items.q: Abdominal part of the ureter: start and course?
items.a: Begins at renal pelvis, runs caudally on a sagittal course

items.q: Pelvic part: direction on entering the pelvic cavity?
items.a: Bends medially

items.q: Ureter enters what in the male? In the female?
items.a: Genital fold (male); broad ligament, specifically mesometrium (female)

items.q: Where do ureters open into the bladder?
items.a: Dorsal surface of the neck of the bladder

items.q: Why do ureters penetrate the bladder wall obliquely?
items.a: Prevents urine reflux into the ureter when intravesical pressure rises

items.q: Why doesn't oblique entry block bladder filling?
items.a: Ureteric peristalsis overcomes the resistance
Pressure within the bladder (vesica = bladder)
Distensible urine storage organ

items.q: Smooth muscle of the bladder wall?
items.a: Detrusor muscle (not identified in lab)
Transitional epithelium (allows distension)

items.q: Three parts of the bladder (cranial → caudal)?
items.a: Apex, body, neck
Cranial blind end; has scar tissue

items.q: Scar on the bladder apex is a remnant of the…
items.a: Urachus
Connects the primitive bladder to the allantoic sac
Narrow caudal part leading into the urethra

items.q: Why is the bladder easy to reach from the ventral abdominal wall?
items.a: Not covered by greater omentum; directly contacts abdominal wall

items.q: Openings of the ureters into the bladder?
items.a: Ureteric orifices
Ureteric (ureter), uterine (uterus), urethral (urethra)

items.q: Trigone of the bladder is formed by…
items.a: Two ureteric orifices plus the urethral crest
Median ridge; male ductus deferens and prostate empty secretions there
Apex scar, lumen, ureteric orifices, trigone, urethral crest, urethra
Three: two lateral and one median
Lateral surface of the bladder to the pelvic wall
Free edge of the lateral ligament

items.q: Round ligament contains the remnant of the…
items.a: Umbilical artery (may stay patent and supply the bladder)
Ventral surface of the bladder to the pelvic symphysis and linea alba

items.q: Median ligament in the fetus contains…
items.a: Urachus and umbilical arteries

items.q: Umbilical cord vessels and their ligament homes?
items.a: Umbilical arteries (bladder ligaments) + umbilical vein (falciform ligament free edge)
Urine only
Urine, semen, and seminal (accessory gland) secretions
Internal opening at bladder neck → external opening at end of penis

items.q: Two parts of the male urethra?
items.a: Pelvic part (internal) and penile part (external)

items.q: Female external urethral orifice opens into the…
items.a: Vagina
Opening of the penile urethra at the end of the penis

traps: Ureteric (ureter) vs uterine (uterus) vs urethral (urethra) orifice: spelling matters.
Hilus = the indented border (door); sinus = the space behind it (garage).
Renal sinus is a 'recess', but pelvic recesses are diverticula of the renal pelvis.
Renal pelvis is a dilated ureter, not bone.
Renal papilla = apex of pyramid; renal crest = fused papillae.
Median section shows the crest; paramedian shows pyramids and papillae.
Right kidney is cranial and fixed; left is caudal ('left behind') and pendulous.
Right kidney medial border faces caudal vena cava; left faces aorta.
Lateral ligament → pelvic wall (round ligament = free edge); median ligament → pelvic symphysis and linea alba.
Ureters enter the bladder dorsally; the urethra leaves from the neck.
